warning: Single-run performance observations unless stated otherwise. Quality scores are orthography-sensitive native-script agreement, not population estimates, semantic-quality scores, hiring validity, or speaker identity.

vibevoice_seeded_repeat_validation.interpretation: On this host, synchronized model.generate() wall time (speech encode + prefill + decode) was 2.66x lower on MPS float32 than CPU float32; MPS bfloat16 was another observed 1.70x lower, but emitted 96 rather than 97 tokens, so this is not a pure dtype-kernel ratio. Fallback-disabled does not prove GPU saturation. The runner job window excludes imports/process startup. Outputs were repeat-stable within a configuration but not equal across device/dtype configurations.

mps_allocator_limit.error: MPS allocated 16.04 GiB with 16.00 GiB maximum

logits_to_keep_seeded_ab.note: Seeded 28-second and 150-second pairs preserved normalized output and were performance-neutral. The optimization removes a concrete prompt-length-scaled full-vocabulary tensor, but the 0.2-second sampler did not resolve a peak-memory difference and there is no measured speed claim.

cantomap_yue_hk_149_9s.reference_unit: Han characters plus alphanumeric spans with internal apostrophes or hyphens

vibevoice_mps_bfloat16_logitskeep.note: Whole-segment control labels are excluded from transcript scoring. The zero-collar value is ELAN-agreement DER, not independently adjudicated diarization ground truth; the 250 ms result is sensitivity-only because dense boundaries leave 57.8% of audio evaluated. MPS driver telemetry is not resident-memory evidence.

cantomap_yue_hk_149_9s.interpretation: VibeVoice required 11 fewer edits (2.89 absolute MER points) and preserved two anonymous speaker labels, but FireRed was faster and much lighter. Traditional/Simplified and Cantonese orthographic variants account for many common substitutions; one conversation does not establish a model-wide dialect winner.

spice_yue_interview_participant_channel_.reference_limit: Interviewer speech is audible but absent from the transcript. VibeVoice speaker 1 is selected by oracle participant-utterance interval overlap; this is not identity recognition, independently adjudicated VAD, or full DER.

vibevoice_mps_bfloat16_logitskeep.note: Full-span structural stability was observed once. Driver allocation includes allocator caches/MPSGraph and is not resident physical memory; live MPS tensor allocation is the defensible lower bound. An unbaselined host-wide swap reading near 40 GiB was observed but is not process-attributable.

spice_yue_interview_participant_channel_.interpretation: On this one participant-microphone interview, runner-reported FireRed wall time was 22.1% lower and it was materially lighter; VibeVoice required 148 fewer transcript edits. Oracle mapping strongly identifies VibeVoice speaker 1 with participant utterance intervals; the other anonymous stream is unscored. The runners do not include exactly the same Python/module-import boundary, so the percentage is configuration-specific. Neither transcript agreement nor interval overlap measures semantic accuracy or behavioral-analysis validity.

spice_yue_exact_repeat_stress_3600s.fixture: Two bit-exact repetitions of the 30-minute participant-microphone audio; stability/resource evidence only
spice_yue_exact_repeat_stress_3600s.interpretation: FireRed sustained faster-than-realtime processing through one hour. Overall peak RSS stayed load-dominated (9.12 GiB at 30m vs 9.15 GiB at 60m), while inference-phase sampled RSS rose from 6.61 to 7.80 GiB (+1.19 GiB / 18.0%); a longer-duration plateau is not established. Exact text and speaker-null sequences repeated; a subset of timestamps moved by 1 ms. Duplicated audio is a deterministic stability gate, not a second accuracy sample or evidence for every hour-long interview.
